title: factory-task-budget
description: Versioned strict generic resource-budget configuration for one implementation task (Phase 2A). The trusted supervisor enforces the budget around every fresh implementation attempt of one selected task: it bounds the cumulative wall time, cumulative process-tree CPU time, combined captured output bytes, and live/descendant process peak, and keeps a per-command timeout as defense-in-depth. The cumulative per-task ledger (factory-task-budget-ledger/v1) is bound to (campaign, selected task) under the ignored .factory-state/ namespace, is updated monotonically after every attempt, and a consumed budget stops further attempts (dirty work is preserved; exhaustion is a non-success outcome and can never produce acceptance). There is no small command-count limit: focused inspect/edit/test/diagnose cycles continue while the resource budgets remain. Every field is a bounded integer, the field set is closed (additionalProperties false), duplicate JSON keys are rejected at parse time, and budget exhaustion is recorded with an explicit closed-enum exhaustion reason.

wall_time_seconds.description: Cumulative wall-clock budget across all implementation attempts of the selected task, in seconds.

cpu_time_seconds.description: Cumulative process CPU budget (user + system across the whole process tree) across all implementation attempts of the selected task, in seconds. The trusted supervisor samples the real /proc utime+stime of the live process tree at a bounded frequency; if accounting cannot be trusted in production the campaign fails closed (accounting_untrusted) instead of running unbounded.

output_bytes.description: Cumulative combined stdout+stderr byte budget across all implementation attempts of the selected task. The trusted supervisor bounds the combined captured streams and terminates the attempt on overflow; truncation can never hide a failure because overflow is a structured non-success outcome, never acceptance.

max_live_processes.description: Maximum live/descendant process count of one implementation attempt. The trusted supervisor terminates the attempt when the live process tree exceeds the bound; the existing subreaper and escaped-descendant cleanup remain authoritative.

per_command_timeout_seconds.description: Defense-in-depth per-command timeout in seconds, delivered to the model as explicit role context. The cumulative resource budgets replace the old three-command cap; the per-command timeout remains as a bounded backpressure floor.
